newsitem.title: EGYPT: Cements, mills drag Egypt shares down.
newsitem.headline: Cements, mills drag Egypt shares down.

text.p: Egyptian share prices slipped back on Wednesday as a new round of selling hit flour mills and cements, the dominant sectors on the exchange.
The Capital Market Authority (CMA) all-share index fell to 349.78 points from 350.68 on Tuesday in about average turnover of 42.04 million pounds ($12.38 million).
Partially privatised Alexandria Flour Mills was the most active share for the second day running. It closed unchanged at 84.99 pounds.

Alone among the other milling shares, Upper Egypt Flour Mills gained in the day's trading. It ended 0.30 up at 77.30. Market analysts Prime Investments recommended on Monday that investors buy the shares at up to 79 pounds ($23.27).
General Silos and Storage, which tracks the milling sector, fell 1.40 to 88.10 pounds.

The three busiest cement stocks were weaker to steady -- Amriyah Cement slipped 0.01 to 82.49 in very active trade, Suez Cement lost 0.99 to close at 66.01 and Helwan Portland Cement HELW.CA ended 0.15 down at 70.50.
Brokers say the market, languishing around six-month lows for several weeks, now contains many bargains but it could be several months before investors wake up to the opportunities.

The banking sector was mixed, with no clear direction. Commercial International Bank/CIB added 0.10 to end the day at 72.60. Misr International Bank/MIBank gained four pounds to close at 582 pounds. Egyptian American lost more than three percent to 122.00.
The index for openly traded firms fell to 474.21 from 475.75 points on Tuesday and that for the rarely traded "closed" firms fell to 259.99 points from 260.57.
Of the 83 shares traded, 30 rose, 29 fell while 24 ended unchanged, the CMA said.
